name: Fancy Fence
description: Everybody knows that Balázs has the fanciest fence in the whole town. It's built up from $$$N$$$ fancy sections. The sections are rectangles standing closely next to each other on the ground. The $$$i$$$th section has integer height $$$h_i$$$ and integer width $$$w_i$$$. We are looking for fancy rectangles on this fancy fence. A rectangle is fancy if: its sides are either horizontal or vertical and have integer lengths the distance between the rectangle and the ground is integer the distance between the rectangle and the left side of the first section is integer it's lying completely on sections What is the number of fancy rectangles? This number can be very big, so we are interested in it modulo $$$10^9+7$$$.
input_specification: The first line contains $$$N$$$ ($$$1\leq N \leq 10^{5}$$$) – the number of sections. The second line contains $$$N$$$ space-separated integers, the $$$i$$$th number is $$$h_i$$$ ($$$1 \leq h_i \leq 10^{9}$$$). The third line contains $$$N$$$ space-separated integers, the $$$i$$$th number is $$$w_i$$$ ($$$1 \leq w_i \leq 10^{9}$$$).
output_specification: You should print a single integer, the number of fancy rectangles modulo $$$10^9+7$$$. So the output range is $$$0,1,2,\ldots, 10^9+6$$$.
approach_summary: Maintain disjoint sets using path compression and union by rank/size. Process edge additions and component queries in O(α(N)) amortized time.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1402A — Fancy Fence [80. DSU / Union Find]
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Connectivity is an equivalence relation. By organizing connected components into trees and merging smaller trees into larger ones (`union-by-rank/size`) combined with path compression, find and union operations run in near-constant inverse Ackermann time $O(\alpha(N))$.
